Original:
Chehlum ko karbala me jo aayi wo bibiyaa
Sadaat e karbala..
Translation:
When the noble ladies came to Karbala on Arba'een,
The ladies of Karbala...

Original:
Har bibi kar rahi thi kuch is tarha se girya
Sadaat e karbala
Translation:
Every lady was mourning in this manner,
The ladies of Karbala...

Original:
Kuch bibiya'n yaha hai kuch bibiya'n waha
Karti hui fughaa
Bikhri hui thi maqtal e sarwar me jaa bajaa
Translation:
Some ladies were here, some were there,
Crying in anguish.
Scattered all across the battlefield of the Master.

Original:
Ek bibi dasht e khooni me jaati hai nahr par
Kehti ba chashme tarr
Abbas dene aayi hoon pursa Sakina ka
Translation:
One lady walked through the blood-soaked plain to the river,
With tear-filled eyes she said,
'Abbas, I have come to offer condolences for Sakina.'

Original:
Ghut ghutke laadli teri zinda mein mar gayi
Turbat wahi'n bani
Bhaiyya wo qaid se na hui marke bhi juda
Translation:
Your beloved little daughter died in the prison, suffocating with grief.
Her grave was made there.
Brother, even in death she was not separated from her captivity.

Original:
Akbar ki qabr par yu hui Laila nauhagar
Dekha na saal bhar
Aayi hu qaid e Shaam se ab hoke mai reha
Translation:
At Akbar's grave, Layla lamented,
'I did not see you for an entire year.
Now I have returned, freed from the captivity of Sham.'

Original:
Bano ye bain karti thi aye mere bezubaa'n
Maa dhoonde ab kahaa
Batla de hai kaha'n mera Asghar aye Karbala
Translation:
Bano cried out,
'O my speechless one,
Where shall your mother search now?
Tell me, O Karbala, where is my Asghar?'

Original:
Qurbaan tere aye mere maa jaaye bewatan
Majboor thi bahen
Zindaa'n mein mujhse teri amanat hui juda
Translation:
May I be sacrificed for you, my homeland-less beloved.
Your sister was helpless.
In the prison, your precious trust was taken from me.

Original:
Rote hai khaas o aam tera sunke ye kalaam
Aye shaah ke ghulaam
Nauha tera Anees hai makbool e baargaah
Translation:
The high and the low alike weep upon hearing these verses.
O servant of the King,
Your elegy, Anees, is accepted in the Divine Court.
